'''''Digitalis thapsi''''', which has been called '''mullein foxglove''' in the US, is a [[flowering plant]] in the genus ''[[Digitalis]]'' that is [[endemic]] to the [[Iberian Peninsula]], where it occurs in eastern [[Portugal]] and central and western [[Spain]]. It is of commercial importance as an [[ornamental plant]]. Hybrids with [[Digitalis purpurea|''D. purpurea'']] have proved successful and are fertile.

==Taxonomy==
It was first [[Species description|described]] in the modern taxonomic system by [[Carl Linnaeus]] in 1763.<ref name=ipni/>

The genus ''[[Digitalis]]'' was formerly assigned to the [[Family (taxonomy)|family]] [[Scrophulariaceae]],<ref name=cabello>{{cite journal|last1=Cabello |first1=M. L. |last2=Ruiz |first2=T. |last3=Devesa |first3=J. A. |title=Carpology, germination and seedling performance in ''Digitalis thapsi'' L. (Scrophulariaceae) |journal=Botanical Journal of Scotland |year=2001 |volume=53 |issue=2 |pages=135–154 |doi=10.1080/03746600108685019|s2cid=84615329}}</ref> but it is now considered to belong within the [[Plantaginaceae]].<ref name=PoWO>{{cite web |title=''Digitalis thapsi'' L. |date=2017 |work=[[Plants of the World Online]] |publisher=[[Royal Botanic Gardens, Kew]] |url=http://powo.science.kew.org/taxon/802092-1 |access-date=23 November 2020}}</ref>

===Hybrids===
[[Joseph Gottlieb Kölreuter]], a German botanist, observed that ''D. thapsi'' had many characteristics of [[Digitalis purpurea|''D. purpurea'']] after four to five generations of cultivation, and that the former became indistinguishable from the latter, a report that was considered "probably" trustworthy by [[Charles Darwin]]. ''D. thapsi'' and ''D. purpurea'' [[Hybrid (biology)|hybrid]]s are generally fertile.<ref name=darwin>{{cite book|last=Stauffer |first=R. C. |title=Charles Darwin's Natural selection : being the second part of his big species book written from 1856 to 1858 |url=https://archive.org/details/charlesdarwinsna1858darw |url-access=limited |year=1987 |publisher=[[Cambridge University Press]] |location=Cambridge |isbn=978-0-521-34807-2 |edition=1, paperback |page=[https://archive.org/details/charlesdarwinsna1858darw/page/n608 127]}}</ref>

In many areas of Spain and Portugal populations of ''D. thapsi'' and ''D. purpurea'' meet, and [[introgression]] is common. These have been known as ''D. purpurea'' [[Nothospecies|nothosubsp.]] ''carpetana'' and [[Digitalis minor|''D. minor'']] in error in two older Portuguese works (1906, 1913), but this hybrid is now generally known as '''''D.'' × ''coutinhoi'''''.<ref name=ibérica>{{cite book |last1=Benedí i Gonzalez |first1=Carles |last2=Hinz Alcaraz |first2=P.-A. |date=15 January 2009 |chapter='''17'''. ''Digitalis'' |chapter-url=http://www.floraiberica.es/floraiberica/texto/pdfs/13_144_17_Digitalis.pdf#page=351 |editor-last=Benedí i Gonzalez |editor-first=Carles |editor-last2=Rico Hernández |editor-first2=Enrique |editor-last3=Güemes Heras |editor-first3=Jaime |editor-last4=Herrero Nieto |editor-first4=Alberto |title=Flora Ibérica, Vol. XIII |url=https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/13746/?offset=#page=1 |language=es |location=Madrid |publisher=Real Jardín Botánico |pages=342–343, 351–353, 357 |isbn=9788400087470}}</ref>

==Description==
[[File:Digitalis thapsi 20100522 1.jpg|thumb|right|Growing in its native Spain]]

===Habitus===
''Digitalis thapsi'' is a [[perennial plant]].<ref name=ibérica/><ref name="Kole2011">{{cite book|last=Kole |first=Chittaranjan |title=Wild Crop Relatives: Genomic and Breeding Resources: Plantation and Ornamental Crops |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=UdDMCfgr4dEC&pg=PA78 |date=1 September 2011 |publisher=Springer Science & Business Media |isbn=978-3-642-21201-7 |pages=78}}</ref> Its yellow-green leaves are ovate to oblong in shape and decurrent, with winged bases.<ref name=kar>{{cite book |last=Kar |first=A. |title=Pharmacognosy And Pharmacobiotechnology |year=2003 |publisher=New Age International Ltd. |location=New Delhi |isbn=978-81-224-1501-8 |page=173}}</ref> The flowers, stems and leaves are covered with a dense [[indumentum]] of tiny hairs, giving them a soft appearance.<ref name=ibérica/><ref name=kar/> These yellow-green hairs ([[trichome]]s) are exclusively glandular. The entire plant is very sticky (glutinose). It is [[caespitose]], meaning it grows with its large leaves tightly arranged into one, or a number, of rosettes growing at or just above ground level. In older plants the base becomes woody and highly branched at ground level, so that a single plant has multiple rosettes. The green, round to slightly angular stems grow to (30-)50 to 80(-100)cm in height before they start to flower. The stems are similarly entirely covered in glandular hairs; these are present in two forms: short and subsessile, or much longer, 0.4 to 0.6mm.<ref name=ibérica/>

The [[karyotype|chromosome count]] is  2''n''=56.<ref name=ibérica/>

===Leaves===
The lower basal leaf blades are 7.5 to 13 cm (exceptionally 19 cm) in length, 2.5 to 5 cm in width, more or less flat but sometimes undulated along the margins, and oblong to elliptic in shape, with a sharp to somewhat sharply tipped apex. The bases of the leaves taper gradually into the [[Petiole (botany)|petioles]]. The texture is soft, not leathery. The underside is [[wikt:rugose#English|rugose]]-reticular in texture, coloured 	greenish-yellow and very densely packed with glandular hairs. The leaves in the middle of the rosette are clearly [[decurrent]]. The margins are denticulate or somewhat so, rarely [[Entire leaf|subentire]].<ref name=ibérica/>

===Flowers===
The pink, rarely white,<ref name=ibérica/> flowers are arranged in an [[inflorescence]] in the form of a [[raceme]],<ref name=database>{{cite web|title=''Digitalis thapsi'' |url=http://www.plantdatabase.co.uk/Digitalis_thapsi |publisher=Plant Database |access-date=2 October 2012 |url-status=dead |archive-url=https://web.archive.org/web/20140106040314/http://www.plantdatabase.co.uk/Digitalis_thapsi |archive-date=6 January 2014}}</ref> 15 to 35 cm in length with 15 to 40 individual flowers. The inflorescence has glandular hairs along its shaft, is not stiff, and is secundiflorous, meaning the flowers follow each other in succession. The flowers have a 1 to 2 cm long [[Pedicel (botany)|pedicel]] which is curved at the base, and shorter to equal in length to the subtending [[bract]]s. The flowers hang somewhat, and are separated by internodes of 8-15mm. The bracts are 12 to 20mm in length and 2 to 3mm broad, glandular and [[lanceolate]] in shape.<ref name=ibérica/>

===Chemistry===
According to Dutch botanist [[Herman Boerhaave]], writing at the turn of the 17th century, ''Digitalis'' species are highly poisonous if directly ingested.<ref>{{cite book|title=Encyclopædia Britannica |volume=4 |year=1823 |publisher=Archibald Constable and Company |location=Edinburgh |edition=6th}}</ref> All parts are poisonous.<ref name=database/><ref name=edinger>{{cite book|last1=Edinger |first1=Philip |last2=Sanchez |first2=Janet H. |date=2002 |title=Annuals and Perennials |url=https://archive.org/details/annualsperennial2002edin |url-access=registration |publisher=Sunset Books |page=[https://archive.org/details/annualsperennial2002edin/page/118 118]}}</ref> In studies, the restriction of [[calcium]] ions resulted in [[cardenolide]] accumulation in ''D. thapsi''.<ref name=cacho2>{{cite journal|last=Cacho|first=M. M.|title=Calcium restriction induces cardenolide accumulation in cell suspension cultures of ''Digitalis thapsi'' L|journal=Plant Cell Reports |year=1995 |volume=14 |issue=12 |pages=786–789 |issn=0721-7714 |display-authors=etal |doi=10.1007/bf00232923 |pmid=24186713 |s2cid=8040006}}</ref> Calcium quantity affects the [[redox]] chemical reactions in the cells. Without calcium, changes in [[antioxidant]] function were observed and [[catalase]] activity was slow.<ref name=paranhos>{{cite journal|last=Paranhos |first=A. |author2=Fernandez-Tarrago, J. |author3=Corchete, P. |title=Relationship between active oxygen species and cardenolide production in cell cultures of ''Digitalis thapsi'': effect of calcium restriction |journal=New Phytologist |date=1 January 1999 |volume=141 |issue=1 |pages=51–60 |doi=10.1046/j.1469-8137.1999.00317.x}}</ref> In another study, lack of calcium retarded growth and promoted [[digoxin]] formation. [[Manganese sulfate]] and [[lithium chloride]] also increased the digoxin concentration, but did not affect growth.<ref name=corchete>{{cite journal|last=Corchete|first=M. P.|title=Effect of calcium, manganese and lithium on growth and cardenolide content in cell suspension cultures of ''Digitalis thapsi'' L. |journal=Plant Cell Reports |date=1 October 1991 |volume=10 |issue=8 |pages=394–396 |doi=10.1007/BF00232609 |pmid=24221731 |s2cid=21383174 |issn=1432-203X |display-authors=etal}}</ref> [[Calcium oxalate]] crystals have also been isolated from ''D. thapsi''.<ref name=kar/><ref name="Prakashan2009">{{cite book |last1=Kokate |first1=C. K. |last2=Gokhale |first2=S. B. |last3=Purohit |first3=A. P. |title=Pharmacognosy |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KwYIsLRyDp4C&pg=SA8-PA39 |year=2009 |publisher=Nirali Prakashan |isbn=978-81-963961-5-2 |pages=39–40 |access-date=31 August 2012}}</ref><ref name=khandewal>{{cite book|last=Khandewal |first=K. R. |title=Practical Pharmacognosy |year=2008 |publisher=Nirali Prakashan |location=Pune |isbn=978-81-85790-30-5 |page=59}}</ref>

===Similar species===
In 1841 [[Pierre Edmond Boissier]] considered it the most similar to [[Digitalis mariana|''D. mariana'']], which he was then describing as a new species, having [[Plant collection|collected]] from the same region.<ref name=Boissier1841>{{cite book |last=Boissier |first=Pierre Edmond |author-link=Pierre Edmond Boissier |date=1841 |title=Voyage botanique dans le midi de l'Espagne |url=https://bibdigital.rjb.csic.es/viewer/9792/?offset=#page=470 |location=Paris |publisher=Gide et Cie. |page=466 |language=fr, la |volume=II }}</ref> In the [[Single-access key|dichotomous key]] in the ''[[Flora Iberica]]'', it is keyed out to ''D. mariana'', [[Digitalis minor|''D. minor'']] and [[Digitalis purpurea|''D. purpurea'']]. ''D. thapsi'' is distinguished from these three other similar species by being the only very sticky species, being completely covered in relatively long, yellowish, glandular hairs. It is also the only species in which the leaves in the middle of the rosette are clearly decurrent. ''D. minor'', an endemic of the [[Balearic Islands]], is not [[sympatric]] with ''D. thapsi''.<ref name=ibérica/>

==Distribution==
''Digitalis thapsi'' is an [[endemic]] species of the [[Iberian Peninsula]],<ref name=EurMed/><ref name=PoWO/> occurring in both [[Portugal]] and [[Spain]]. It grows in the mountains and rocky plains of the central and central-western parts of the Iberian Peninsula, especially in the [[Sistema Central]] and its extensions between the rivers of the [[Douro]] and [[Tagus]].<ref name=ibérica/>

It is widespread in Spain,<ref name=cabello/> occurring in the western and central parts of the country.<ref name=PoWO/><ref name=grin>{{GRIN | accessdate = 21 January 2018}}</ref><ref name=catlf>{{cite web |last=Hassler |first=M. |date=November 2018 |title=Synonymic Checklists of the Vascular Plants of the World, Species Details : ''Digitalis thapsi'' L. |url=http://www.catalogueoflife.org/col/details/species/id/cba2c55f78105002a599b1deabf6da32 |website=World Plants |publisher=Digital resource at www.catalogueoflife.org/col |issn=2405-8858 |access-date=21 November 2020}}</ref> It does not occur on the [[Balearic Islands]].<ref name=EurMed/> It occurs in the provinces of [[province of Ávila|Ávila]], [[Province of Badajoz|Badajoz]], [[Province of Cáceres|Cáceres]], [[Province of Córdoba (Spain)|Córdoba]], [[Province of Guadalajara|Guadalajara]], [[Community of Madrid|Madrid]], [[Province of Salamanca|Salamanca]], [[Province of Segovia|Segovia]], [[Province of Soria|Soria]], [[Province of Toledo|Toledo]] and [[Province of Zamora|Zamora]]. It has incidentally been found in the [[province of Burgos]].<ref name=ibérica/> In [[Andalucía]] it is only found in the north of the region, in the western [[Sierra Morena]], where it is uncommon;<ref name=Andalucía>{{cite book |last1=Cabezudo |first1=B. |last2=Talavera |first2=S. |last3=Blanca |first3=G. |last4=Salazar |first4=C. |last5=Cueto |first5=M. J. |last6=Valdés |first6=B. |last7=Hernández Bermejo |first7=J. E. |last8=Herrera |first8=C. |last9=Rodríguez Hiraldo |first9=C. |last10=Navas |first10=D. |date=2005 |title=Lista roja de la flora vascular de Andalucía |url=http://www.anthos.es/docs/Phyteia/LYL_AND_02.pdf |location=Sevilla |publisher=Consejería de Medio Ambiente, Junta de Andalucía |page=32 |language=es |isbn=84-96329-62-3}}</ref> it has been collected more often in the mountains of central Spain.<ref name=anthos/><ref name=ibérica/>

In Portugal it primarily occurs in the northern and central interior,<ref name=PoWO/><ref name=catlf/> more precisely in the districts of [[Bragança District|Bragança]], [[Vila Real District|Vila Real]], [[Guarda District|Guarda]], [[Viseu District|Viseu]], [[Castelo Branco District|Castelo Branco]], [[Portalegre District|Portalegre]] and [[Évora District|Évora]]. With less frequency, it has also been found in the [[Porto District|Porto]], [[Aveiro District|Aveiro]], [[Coimbra District|Coimbra]], [[Santarém District|Santarém]], [[Beja District|Beja]] and [[Faro (Portuguese district)|Faro]] Districts.<ref name=ibérica/><ref>{{cite web |title=Digitalis thapsi L. |url=https://flora-on.pt/#1Digitalis+thapsi |publisher=[[Flora-On]] |access-date=2 August 2022}}</ref>

==Ecology==
''Digitalis thapsi'' grows in acidic soils.<ref name=Andalucía/> It grows on rocky ground<ref name=ibérica/><ref name=Andalucía/> and on slopes. It prefers sunny, open and disturbed places. It generally grows on soils derived from [[granite]], but also sometimes on [[quartzite]] and [[schist]]. It grows at (rarely 100-) 500–1500 metres in altitude.<ref name=ibérica/>

The specific [[phytosociology|phytosociological]] [[Association (ecology)|suballiance]] and alliance wherein it occurs is called 'Rumici indurati-Dianthion lusitani', which is in the order 'Phagnalo saxatilis-Rumicetalia indurati', in the class 'Phagnalo saxatilis-Rumicetea indurati'. It is a characteristic species of this phytocoenosis. In this [[habitat]] it occurs together with these following characteristic species: [[Antirrhinum graniticum|''Antirrhinum graniticum'' subsp. ''graniticum'']], ''[[Antirrhinum rupestris]]'', ''[[Arrhenatherum fernandesii]]'', ''[[Biscutella bilbilitana]]'', [[Centaurea monticola|''Centaurea monticola'' subsp. ''citricolor'']], ''[[Centaurea pinnata]]'', ''[[Coincya leptocarpa]]'', ''[[Coincya longirostra]]'', [[Coincya pseudoerucastrum|''Coincya pseudoerucastrum'' subsp. ''pseudoerucastrum'']], ''[[Coincya rupestris]]'', [[Conopodium bunioides|''Conopodium bunioides'' subsp. ''aranii'']], [[Conopodium majus|''Conopodium majus'' subsp. ''marizianum'']], ''[[Crepis oporinoides]]'', [[Dianthus crassipes|''Dianthus crassipes'' subsp. ''crassipes'']], [[Dianthus crassipes|''Dianthus crassipes'' subsp. ''sereneanus'']], ''[[Dianthus lusitanus]]'', ''[[Digitalis mariana]]'' (both subspecies), [[Digitalis purpurea|''Digitalis purpurea'' subsp. ''toletana'']], ''[[Erodium mouretti]]'', [[Erysimum linifolium|''Erysimum linifolium'' subsp. ''lagascae'']], ''[[Festuca duriotagana]]'', [[Jasione sessiliflora|''Jasione sessiliflora'' subsp. ''tomentosa'']], ''[[Scrophularia oxyrhincha]]'', ''[[Scrophularia sublyrata]]'', [[Sedum hirsutum|''Sedum hirsutum'' subsp. ''baeticum'']], ''[[Silene marizii]]'', ''[[Silene × montistellensis]]'' and [[Verbascum rotundifolium|''Verbascum rotundifolium'' subsp. ''castellanum'']].<ref name=Menéndez2017>{{cite web |url=https://www.asturnatura.com/especie/digitalis-thapsi.html |title=Num. 622: ''Digitalis thapsi'' L. |last=Menéndez Valderrey |first=Juan Luis |date=27 February 2017 |website=Asturnatura.com |publisher=AsturnaturaDB |language=es |issn=1887-5068 |access-date=24 November 2020}}</ref>

In its native lands it flowers from June to July.<ref name=ibérica/> In cultivation it flowers in late spring<ref name="MBG"/><ref name=database/> to early summer.<ref name="MBG"/> A study of the fruiting activity in ''D. thapsi'' showed that production, size and number of seeds were interrelated. Analysis has shown that seed weight is not related to the length of the [[cotyledon]], and that the length of the fifth leaf can serve as a useful factor in determining the [[genetic variability]] among specimens.<ref name=cabello/>

==Uses==
===Agriculture===
It is known that [[livestock]] avoid eating this plant, but an exception are goats, which will eat the leaves and flowers in times of shortage. Nonetheless, the plant is poisonous for them, causing stupor and paralysis -this was apparently once not an uncommon occurrence in Spain, and has spawned a number of idioms.<ref name=González2018>{{cite book |last1=González |first1=José Antonio |last2=Vallejo |first2=José Ramón |last3=Amich |first3=Francisco |date=May 2018 |chapter=''Digitalis thapsi'' L. |chapter-url=https://www.researchgate.net/publication/325335939 |editor1-last=Pardo de Santayana |editor1-first=Manuel |editor2-last=Morales |editor2-first=Ramón |editor3-last=Tardío |editor3-first=Javier |editor4-last=Molina |editor4-first=Maria |title=Inventario Español de los Conocimientos Tradicionales Relativos a la Biodiversidad |language=es |publisher=Ministerio de Agricultura y Pesca, Alimentación y Medio Ambiente (MAPAMA) |volume=II |edition=1 |pages=312–313 }}</ref>

===Cultivation===
The species is used as a perennial, [[ornamental plant]].<ref name="Kole2011"/> It is low-growing, so is used in the border. It grows well in half-shaded to sun-exposed areas in temperate regions.<ref name="MBG"/><ref name=database/> It prefers organically rich, reasonably well-drained, acidic soils. In Missouri it is said to require constantly moist soil.<ref name="MBG"/> In British gardens moderate watering is required; the plant has an average drought tolerance,<ref name=database/> and is adaptable to dry shady areas.<ref name="CullenKnees2011">{{cite book|last1=Cullen |first1=James |last2=Knees |first2=Sabina G. |last3=Cubey |first3=H. Suzanne |last4=Shaw |first4=J. M. H. |title=The European Garden Flora Flowering Plants: A Manual for the Identification of Plants Cultivated in Europe, Both Out-of-Doors and Under Glass |url=https://books.google.com/books?id=KLPcml_QiFQC&pg=PA211 |date=11 August 2011 |publisher=Cambridge University Press |isbn=978-0-521-76164-2 |pages=211}}</ref> It is tolerant of deer. Many gardeners remove the spent flower spikes soon after bloom, not allowing it to go to seed.<ref name="MBG"/>

Besides normal cultivation, ''D. thapsi'' has been propagated using [[explant culture]], a technique employed by isolating and harvesting [[meristem]] cells from pieces of tissue. [[Auxin]]s [[1-naphthaleneacetic acid|NAA]], 2,4-D and [[Indole-3-acetic acid|IAA]] alone or combined with [[kinetin|BA]] produced a [[Callus (cell biology)|callus]]. NAA caused root formation and BA shoot formation. NAA and BA combined induced organ generation more effectively. Plantlets obtained this way had a survival rate of 70%.<ref name=cacho>{{cite journal|last1=Cacho |first1=Margarita |last2=Morán |first2=Margarita |last3=Herrera |first3=María Teresa |last4=Fernández-Tárrago |first4=Jorge |title=Morphogenesis in leaf, hypocotyl and root explants of ''Digitalis thapsi'' L. cultured in vitro |journal=Plant Cell, Tissue and Organ Culture |date=May 1991 |volume=25 |issue=2 |pages=117–23 |doi=10.1007/BF00042182 |s2cid=41305774 }}</ref>

A [[cultivar]] called 'Spanish Peaks' with raspberry-rose-coloured flowers and a compact habitus has been available in the US.<ref name="MBG"/>

===Traditional===
In Spain the traditional uses have practically been abandoned. Recorded traditional uses are often identical to that those of ''D. purpurea''; when questioned many informants in Salamanca believed that these were in fact the same species. It is generally thought that the difference in flower colour is due to some characteristic of the soil. Local people are aware it is poisonous. It was once locally used in [[herbalism]] as a cardiac tonic in many places. Other folk medicinal uses are local to specific cities or villages: in the hills near Salamanca the leaves were steeped in water to use for a sore throat or a [[decoction]] used for infected wounds, in a town in [[Galicia (Spain)|Galicia]] the flowers in water were used to combat inflammations, in the provinces of Zamora and Salamanca boils are said to heal after applying a [[poultice]] of the burnt basal leaves.<ref name=González2018/>

==Conservation==
It is not considered rare in a national or international perspective,<ref name=anthos/> but it has been classified as locally '[[endangered]]' in the [[Regional Red List]] of Andalucía of 2005.<ref name=anthos/><ref name=Andalucía/> The reason for this was that the different collection localities and populations in this region were fragmented and very small.<ref name=Andalucía/>
